2027-06-17.title: Thursday of the Eleventh Week in Ordinary Time
readings: I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ
Your works, O Lord, are justice and truth
Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven
2027-06-17.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 11 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-06-17.verse: Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
theo: In the last chapters of the Second Letter to the Corinthians St Paul defends his ministry against some visiting preachers whom he calls, with irony, “super-apostles.” They were eloquent, they demanded payment, and they belittled Paul. He hates to boast, so he asks the Corinthians to put up with “a little foolishness.” Then he opens his heart: “I feel a divine jealousy for you, for I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” In the customs of the time, a friend of the family arranged a betrothal and kept the bride safe until the wedding. Paul sees himself as that friend: he brought the Corinthians to Christ, and he wants to present them to their Bridegroom with an undivided heart. His fear is that “as the serpent deceived Eve by its cunning, your thoughts will be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ.” The danger is “another Jesus,” “a different spirit,” “a different gospel.” The Church has always loved this image of herself as the virgin bride of Christ, and the Fathers saw its perfect fulfilment in the Blessed Virgin Mary, whose heart was wholly given to God (Lumen Gentium 63–64). Paul also explains why he never took money from the Corinthians: he “proclaimed God's good news” to them without charge, supported by the brothers from Macedonia, so that no one could say he preached for profit. And why? “Because I do not love you? God knows I do!”

In the Gospel Jesus teaches his disciples how to pray. First he warns against a mistake: “When you are praying, do not heap up empty phrases as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard because of their many words.” Prayer is not a machine in which more words produce more results. “Your Father knows what you need before you ask him.” Then why pray at all? Because prayer is not informing God; it is being with him as children with a Father, and letting our hearts be formed by his. So Jesus gives the prayer that has been on Christian lips ever since: “Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.” The first three petitions are about God: his name, his kingdom, his will. Only then come our needs: “Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And do not bring us to the time of trial, but rescue us from the evil one.” Tertullian called this prayer “the summary of the whole Gospel” (Catechism 2761), and the early Christians prayed it three times a day (Didache 8). Jesus adds a comment on one petition only, the one about forgiveness: “For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.” We cannot pray “Our Father” with a closed heart towards our brothers and sisters.
outline: Pray the Our Father very slowly together, pausing after each line. Ask: which line was hardest to mean?
Point 1 · A sincere and pure devotion
Paul's divine jealousy for a Church betrothed to Christ alone.
Your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
His name, his kingdom, his will first; then bread, forgiveness and deliverance.
“Your Father knows what you need before you ask him.”
live: Name one thing that draws your heart away from a sincere devotion to Christ, and give it to him today.
Once today, pray the Lord's Prayer as slowly as you can, giving a full breath to each petition.
2027-06-17.prayer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name; your kingdom come; your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Keep us, your Church, a chaste bride for your Son, faithful to the one Jesus, the one Spirit and the one Gospel we have received. Give us today the bread we need, the bread of the earth and the Bread of life. Forgive us as we forgive those who have wronged us, and do not bring us to the time of trial, but rescue us from the evil one. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At every Mass, just before Communion, the priest invites us: at the Saviour's command and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say: Our Father. The Lord's Prayer is the table grace of the Eucharist: we ask for our daily bread just before we receive the Bread of life, and we ask forgiveness before we give one another the sign of peace and approach the altar as reconciled children.

quick: Paul feels a divine jealousy for the Corinthians: he has promised them as a chaste virgin to Christ, and fears they may be led away to another Jesus or a different gospel.
He preached to them without asking for support, because he loves them.
Jesus warns against empty words in prayer, teaches the Our Father, and says that the Father forgives us as we forgive others.
2027-06-17.action: Pray the Our Father once today very slowly, and forgive someone at the words “as we also have forgiven.”
2027-06-17.question: When I pray the Our Father, do I mean the words, especially “your will be done” and “as we forgive”?

family.explain: Jesus' friends asked him: how should we pray? He taught them the prayer we call the Our Father. We do not need to use many words, because God already knows what we need. First we praise God and ask for his kingdom to come; then we ask for food, for forgiveness and for protection from evil. And Jesus says: if we want God to forgive us, we must forgive others.
family.intention: We pray for all who are learning to pray: little children, catechumens, and those who have forgotten how.
family.ask: Ask: “Which line of the Our Father is your favourite, and why?” Then pray it together holding hands.

illus: A young mother in Bengaluru was teaching her four-year-old son the Our Father. When they came to “give us this day our daily bread,” the boy stopped and asked: why do we ask God for bread, when Appa buys it from the shop? The mother thought for a moment, then took him to the window. She showed him the rain falling on the trees, the vendor pushing his cart of vegetables, the bus driver taking his father to work. All of this, she said, is how God gives us bread. Appa works, but God gives him strength, and rain, and work to do. The boy prayed the line again, slowly, and added on his own: and give bread to that man too, pointing at a beggar on the corner. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Teach us to pray as children, with few words and full hearts. Amen.
share: I feel a divine jealousy for you (2 Corinthians 11:2). Is my heart undivided in its love for Christ?
Your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:8). Do I trust the Father with my needs?
If you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). Whom do I need to forgive before I can pray the Our Father honestly?
pm.resp: Your works, O Lord, are justice and truth.
interc: For the Church, the bride of Christ, that she may remain faithful to the one Gospel.
For those who have no daily bread, and for those who share theirs.
For all who are tempted, that the Father may rescue them from the evil one.
For those who find it hard to pray, and for children learning the Our Father.
For our group, that we may pray with sincere hearts and forgive one another.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to call you Our Father. Hear the prayer we make in his words, and make us one family of forgiven and forgiving children. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul speaks today like a loving father of the bride: I feel a divine jealousy for you, for I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ (2 Corinthians 11:2). The Church is the bride of Christ. Each of us, by Baptism, belongs to him. Paul's fear is that our hearts may be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ (2 Corinthians 11:3), by another gospel, by false teachers, by the attractions of the world.

How do we keep our hearts for Christ? Above all, by prayer. And in the Gospel Jesus teaches us how to pray. He says: do not heap up empty phrases, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:7–8). Sometimes we think that the longer our prayer, the more God will listen. But God is not tired by our words or impressed by them. He is our Father. He wants our hearts.

Then Jesus gives us the Our Father. Notice the order. First: hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done. Only after that: give us bread, forgive us, protect us. When we put God first, our own needs find their right place. And notice that we say our Father, not my Father. We never pray alone; we pray as one family.

Finally, Jesus explains only one line: the line about forgiveness. If you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses (Matthew 6:15). Every time we pray the Our Father, we are asking God to forgive us in the same way we forgive. Today, let us pray it slowly, and let us mean it, especially those difficult words: as we forgive those who trespass against us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus taught us a very special prayer: the Our Father. Do you know it by heart? Jesus said we do not need to use lots and lots of words, because God already knows what we need. In the Our Father we call God our Daddy in heaven! We ask him for food, we say sorry, and we promise to forgive others. Tonight, pray it slowly with your family, and think about each word.

intro: Theme: “Your Father knows what you need before you ask him.”
A Church betrothed to Christ alone, prayer without empty words, and the prayer that sums up the Gospel.

sub: Paul as friend of the Bridegroom.
q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy.
I feel a divine jealousy for you, for I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises privately this week, and name one false god you want to renounce.

q: Never be rash with your mouth, nor let your heart be quick to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven, and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few.

When you are praying, do not heap up empty phrases as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard because of their many words. Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silent prayer each day this week, saying only: Father, you know.

sub: His name, his kingdom, his will.
q: For you are our father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us; you, O Lord, are our father; our Redeemer from of old is your name.
Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
points.apply: Pray the Our Father as a family every evening this week, slowly, and forgive one another before you begin.

concl: Paul longs to keep the Church a chaste bride for Christ; prayer keeps our hearts undivided.
Jesus teaches us to pray with few words and a child's trust, putting the Father first and forgiving as we are forgiven.
2027-06-17.resolve: Pray the Our Father slowly every day this week, and mean every word.
